question.prompt: The number \(21!\) \(=51{,}090{,}942{,}171{,}709{,}440{,}000\) has over \(60{,}000\) positive integer divisors. One of them is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is odd?

solutions.title: Group divisors by odd part
solutions.explanation:
Group the divisors by their odd part. Within each group, only the power of \(2\) changes.

First find the exponent of \(2\) in \(21!\). Each multiple of \(2\) contributes one factor of \(2\), each multiple of \(4\) contributes another, and so on. Thus the exponent is
\[
\left\lfloor\frac{21}{2}\right\rfloor+
\left\lfloor\frac{21}{4}\right\rfloor+
\left\lfloor\frac{21}{8}\right\rfloor+
\left\lfloor\frac{21}{16}\right\rfloor
=10+5+2+1=18.
\]
Write \(21!=2^{18}k\), where \(k\) is odd.

Every positive divisor has a unique form \(2^i b\), where \(0\le i\le18\) and \(b\) divides \(k\). For each fixed \(b\), the group
\[
b,\ 2b,\ 2^2b,\ \ldots,\ 2^{18}b
\]
contains \(19\) divisors, exactly one of which, \(b\), is odd. These groups contain every divisor exactly once.

Therefore the probability is \(\boxed{\frac{1}{19}}\), choice B.
